newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda's September coffee exports rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Uganda's September coffee exports rise sharply.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports for the month of September rose sharply over August as harvests improved due to good weather and a new prolific coffee variety, the industry's top body said on Monday.
Uganda is Africa's largest coffee producer and exports from the crop earn it 70 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.
The state Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said in a report coffee exports in September reached 371,324 60-kg bags, up from the 338,614 bags exported in August.

"The generally good weather in coffee-growing areas, that helped the crop to respond to good husbandry practices and made it possible for the crop to be picked all the year round, was responsible," UCDA said.
"The coming into production of clonal coffee planted three to four years ago also helped," it added.
Uganda's coffee exports have been rising since the removal of a coffee tax in June which enabled some exporters to break-even, despite declining international prices.
Finance minister Jehoash Mayanja-Nkangi abolished the 25-percent stabilisation tax on all coffee sold at over 1,500 shillings ($1.60 then) per kg in his budget speech on June 15.
The September exports were higher than those in the same month of 1995 when 284,650 bags were exported.

The rise in exports pushed up Uganda's hard currency earnings from the crop to $30.61 million in September, up from $27.5 million in August, the UCDA, the coffee industry's top policy and monitoring body, said.
The September exports raised to 4,148,803 bags the cumulative figure for the crop year (October-September) which earned $388,916,157 in hard currency, UCDA said.
The year's exports were higher than those for the 1994/95 crop year when the East African country exported 2.76 million bags earning some $433 million, UCDA records show.
The UCDA report, passed to Reuters in Kampala, did not have forecasts for October.

In the absence of major shifts in world prices, local farmgate prices remained stable at between 450 and 550 shillings during the month under review. In August they averaged 400-500 Ugandan shillings, UCDA said.

The Ugandan authority did not say how much coffee was sold in each of the two categories -- arabica, which fetches a higher price on the world market but which accounts for only 12 percent of Uganda's production and the higher-yielding robusta.
